content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will officially launch for all users on Monday, September 14.

In addition, the company also stated that two features originally in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be introduced in a "future software update" for iPhone, including the suggested feature in Messages, and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated its company website this week to reflect that these two features have been temporarily pulled from iOS 27. The relevant changes also apply to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had earlier noticed that the automatic password changing feature was removed in iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm this change.

As a recap, the suggested feature in the Messages app will add information to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with just a tap, based on the content of the user's conversation.

The following is Apple's description of the Passwords feature:

The Passwords app will attempt to go directly to websites where the user has weak or compromised passwords and automatically update them. At WWDC, Apple explained that this feature would use Apple Intelligence and Safari to "take action on the user's behalf in an agent-like manner".

Currently, there are no further details on when these two features will be reintroduced in iOS 27. Apple's website simply states that the relevant features will be provided in a "future software update".
